# Phase 8: method check on a public dataset (generated by scripts/run_phase8_public_check.py)

**This is a check of the modelling METHOD, not of the AI Defence System.** The public data has no sessions, devices, payees or graph.

Data: 284,807 transactions, 492 frauds (prevalence 0.1727%), time range 0-172792 s (about 48 hours). Split [0.6, 0.2, 0.2] = train / validation (used only for calibration) / test. Seed 42. Raw `Time` is not a feature.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Time split vs random split (XGBoost raw)

Average precision: time 0.778 vs random 0.881 (difference +0.103); recall @0.5% alerts: time 0.813 vs random 0.909. The two test sets contain different numbers of frauds (75 vs 99), so part of any gap is just a different test set. Compare the difference with the bootstrap intervals above before calling it real: test sets contain only tens of frauds.

## Leakage control (labels shuffled in training)

Average precision on the true test labels: 0.0018 (per repeat 0.0010, 0.0035, 0.0008) vs test prevalence 0.0013. A value near the prevalence means the pipeline is not leaking labels; a clearly higher value would mean it is.

| test block | train rows | test rows | frauds in test | average precision | recall @0.5% alerts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 94,936 | 47,468 | 52 | 0.740 | 0.788 |
| 3 | 142,404 | 47,468 | 101 | 0.822 | 0.881 |
| 4 | 189,872 | 47,468 | 61 | 0.790 | 0.820 |
| 5 | 237,340 | 47,467 | 61 | 0.763 | 0.820 |

Small fraud counts per block make single-block numbers noisy; look at the spread, not any one row.

## What each outcome would and would not mean

- Calibration: if raw XGBoost has the lowest Brier / ECE here too, that REPEATS the Phase 1 finding on real data; if calibration helps, say so and explain the difference (real data, 0.17% prevalence, much more training data).
- Time vs random: a small gap means this dataset cannot show ordering effects in two days; it does not show that ordering never matters.
- XGBoost vs logistic regression: report the gap honestly; on PCA features a linear model can be strong.
- Whatever the scores, this says nothing about the layered system, the graph stage, the GenAI-era families or the simulator's realism.

## Limits

- About two days of data; no card / customer id (customer-grouped splits impossible); PCA-anonymised features; tens of frauds per block; bootstrap over rows ignores dependence.
- Hyper-parameters are the project's Stage 2 settings, not tuned for this data; `tree_method=hist` instead of `exact` for speed.
